1200: class CrossEntropyLoss(_WeightedLoss):
1201:     r"""This criterion computes the cross entropy loss between input logits
1202:     and target.
1203: 
1204:     It is useful when training a classification problem with `C` classes.
1205:     If provided, the optional argument :attr:`weight` should be a 1D `Tensor`
1206:     assigning weight to each of the classes.
1207:     This is particularly useful when you have an unbalanced training set.
1208: 
1209:     The `input` is expected to contain the unnormalized logits for each class (which do `not` need
1210:     to be positive or sum to 1, in general).
1211:     `input` has to be a Tensor of size :math:`(C)` for unbatched input,
1212:     :math:`(minibatch, C)` or :math:`(minibatch, C, d_1, d_2, ..., d_K)` with :math:`K \geq 1` for the
1213:     `K`-dimensional case. The last being useful for higher dimension inputs, such
1214:     as computing cross entropy loss per-pixel for 2D images.
1215: 
1216:     The `target` that this criterion expects should contain either:
1217: 
1218:     - Class indices in the range :math:`[0, C)` where :math:`C` is the number of classes; if
1219:       `ignore_index` is specified, this loss also accepts this class index (this index
1220:       may not necessarily be in the class range). The unreduced (i.e. with :attr:`reduction`
1221:       set to ``'none'``) loss for this case can be described as:
1222: 
1223:       .. math::
1224:           \ell(x, y) = L = \{l_1,\dots,l_N\}^\top, \quad
1225:           l_n = - w_{y_n} \log \frac{\exp(x_{n,y_n})}{\sum_{c=1}^C \exp(x_{n,c})}
1226:           \cdot \mathbb{1}\{y_n \not= \text{ignore\_index}\}
1227: 
1228:       where :math:`x` is the input, :math:`y` is the target, :math:`w` is the weight,
1229:       :math:`C` is the number of classes, and :math:`N` spans the minibatch dimension as well as
1230:       :math:`d_1, ..., d_k` for the `K`-dimensional case. If
1231:       :attr:`reduction` is not ``'none'`` (default ``'mean'``), then
1232: 
1233:       .. math::
1234:           \ell(x, y) = \begin{cases}
1235:               \sum_{n=1}^N \frac{1}{\sum_{n=1}^N w_{y_n} \cdot \mathbb{1}\{y_n \not= \text{ignore\_index}\}} l_n, &
1236:                \text{if reduction} = \text{`mean';}\\
1237:                 \sum_{n=1}^N l_n,  &
1238:                 \text{if reduction} = \text{`sum'.}
1239:             \end{cases}
1240: 
1241:       Note that this case is equivalent to applying :class:`~torch.nn.LogSoftmax`
1242:       on an input, followed by :class:`~torch.nn.NLLLoss`.
1243: 
1244:     - Probabilities for each class; useful when labels beyond a single class per minibatch item
1245:       are required, such as for blended labels, label smoothing, etc. The unreduced (i.e. with
1246:       :attr:`reduction` set to ``'none'``) loss for this case can be described as:
1247: 
1248:       .. math::
1249:           \ell(x, y) = L = \{l_1,\dots,l_N\}^\top, \quad
1250:           l_n = - \sum_{c=1}^C w_c \log \frac{\exp(x_{n,c})}{\sum_{i=1}^C \exp(x_{n,i})} y_{n,c}
1251: 
1252:       where :math:`x` is the input, :math:`y` is the target, :math:`w` is the weight,
1253:       :math:`C` is the number of classes, and :math:`N` spans the minibatch dimension as well as
1254:       :math:`d_1, ..., d_k` for the `K`-dimensional case. If
1255:       :attr:`reduction` is not ``'none'`` (default ``'mean'``), then
1256: 
1257:       .. math::
1258:           \ell(x, y) = \begin{cases}
1259:               \frac{\sum_{n=1}^N l_n}{N}, &
1260:                \text{if reduction} = \text{`mean';}\\
1261:                 \sum_{n=1}^N l_n,  &
1262:                 \text{if reduction} = \text{`sum'.}
